mira_customer: Hey team — running embeddings API and suddenly getting 1024-dim vectors instead of the 1536 we've always seen. Started yesterday after we rotated keys. Request looks the same on our side. Anyone else seeing this?

alex_support: Hey @mira_customer — sorry about that. Can you paste a redacted request (headers + model param) and the response dims? Also which project/org are you using?

mira_customer: Sure — project: acme-ml, org: acme-inc. Request header snippet: `Authorization: Bearer proj-XXX` and `X-Org-Key: org-YYY`. Body: `{
  "model": "embed-lr-small",
  "input": ["foo"]
}` Response: `{"data":[{"embedding":[...1024 values...] } ]}`

alex_support: Thanks. Quick question — did you switch to using org-level keys recently? I know some flows changed how we prefer auth headers.

mira_customer: Yes rotated to org key last week so billing is consolidated. We were told project keys still work.

alex_support: Copy. Reproducing now in a sandbox — if I use org key with the same model param I get 1536 dims in my test. Can you run a curl with `-v` and paste full headers (you can redact tokens) so we can see exact header names? Example:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer org-YYY" \
  -H "X-Project-Key: proj-XXX" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-lr-small","input":["test"]}'
```

mira_customer: Pasted — we actually set header `Org: org-YYY` (no X- prefix) because our infra strips some headers. Full list: `Authorization: Bearer proj-XXX`, `Org: org-YYY`, `Model: embed-lr-small`.

alex_support: Aha. That might be it. Our routing expects `X-Org-Key` or `X-Org` (legacy `Org-Id`) headers for org override; an unprefixed `Org` header may be getting treated as a custom header and ignored. But odd that it falls back to a 1024-dim model — that implies it's selecting a different embedding family.

jon_eng: Jumping in — paging in from eng-runtime. We recently merged a change that re-ordered auth header precedence to prioritize `Authorization` project tokens over some org headers for security reasons. If the org header isn't recognized (e.g., `Org` vs `X-Org-Key`) the auth chain falls back to the token namespace, which may map to a different default model (older projects use `embed-sm` with 1024 dims).

mira_customer: So because we sent `Authorization: Bearer proj-XXX` and the `Org` header wasn't recognized, the request was authenticated as the project token and used the project's default model mapping? That would explain it.

jon_eng: Exactly. Repro steps I used in staging:
1) `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer proj-OLD" -d '{"model":"embed-lr-small","input":["a"]}'` -> returns 1024 dims
2) `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer org-YYY" -H "X-Project-Key: proj-OLD" ...` -> returns 1536 dims
3) `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer proj-OLD" -H "Org: org-YYY" ...` -> returns 1024 dims (because `Org` not recognized)

ruth_sre: From ops perspective, we saw an alert when a small set of requests started hitting the older embedding family after the auth change rolled out on 2026-03-10. It's low volume but clear signal. Rolling back precedence would be a security regression, but we need a fix that accepts common header shapes.

alex_support: For an immediate workaround, can you send the org key as `X-Org-Key` or put it in Authorization as the org token? If you can't change headers easily, we can add a temporary header mapping on the edge to map `Org`->`X-Org-Key` for your tenant.

mira_customer: We can change outgoing header naming quickly, but we rely on some proxies that drop `X-` headers. Putting org token in Authorization is risky for us. If you can do an edge mapping that'd be ideal.

jon_eng: I'll prepare a quick edge rule to map `Org` to `X-Org-Key` for requests where `Authorization` contains `proj-` and `Org` present. It's low blast radius and reversible.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued by jon_eng — edge-rule:map-org-header-1812345678 — ETA 15m

alex_support: In parallel, we'll open a support ticket and flag billing: some requests authenticated to the project token might be billed to the wrong project. @ruth_sre can you check if any usage spikes align to this tenant?

ruth_sre: Looking now — I see ~1200 embedding calls in last 48h billed to proj-XXX that should've gone to acme-ml. I'll flag for accounting and create a billing adjustment request.

jon_eng: Edge rule live on canary edge. @mira_customer can you retry your same request (with your current headers) and confirm?

mira_customer: Retried — still 1024 dims. Response headers show `x-edge-mapped: Org->X-Org-Key`? Wait I do see that response header now. But dims still 1024.

jon_eng: Hmm. That suggests mapping occurred but downstream auth cache or token resolution happened before edge mapping. I'll check the auth pipeline ordering — maybe we need to escalate to auth-team to accept mapped headers earlier.

alex_support: In the short term I can proxy your requests through our support proxy which injects the org token correctly so you get 1536 dims. Would you like that until we have a durable fix?

mira_customer: Yes please — that would unblock us for today. Also please escalate billing adjustment.

jon_eng: Filed internal bug: RT-embed-auth-precedence-4721. Assigned to @auth-team, priority P1. Plan: ensure `Org` and common variants accepted, make header mapping upstream in ingress, and add unit tests for header precedence. Also add a migration note for teams rotating to org keys.

alex_support: I'll keep this thread updated. Next steps: (1) support-proxy for mira_customer — created and keys exchanged via secure channel; (2) billing adjustment ticket filed; (3) eng/infra fix tracked in RT-embed-auth-precedence-4721. Sorry for the disruption :/ :heart:

mira_customer: Thanks all — appreciate the fast response. Will confirm once we've validated embeddings in prod.

alex_support: Marking this thread as escalated to eng. Will update when RT number changes or fix deployed globally. :thumbsup:
